title: Health and lifestyle
subtitle: superfoods, keeping fit, stress
summary: Talk about what you eat and how you live - healthy and unhealthy foods, superfoods and their benefits, fitness, stress and obesity.

lesson.heading: Diet: healthy and not so healthy
rows: food with a high fat or high salt content
lesson.note: fizzy = with a lot of bubbles; content = the amount that is in the food; wholemeal = containing all the grain, with nothing taken out; processed = treated with chemicals to preserve the food or add taste or colour

lesson.heading: Talking about what we eat
lesson.text: Some foods are considered good for our health. Others can cause **long-term** health problems if they are **consumed** in large **quantities**.

examples.text: Certain foods are **considered** by scientists to be good for our bodies.
Foods with a **high fat content** may cause health problems.
If people eat these foods in **large quantities**, it may be dangerous.
Some foods may cause **long-term** health problems.
examples.note: long-term = lasting a long time into the future; consume = eat (formal)

lesson.heading: Superfoods
lesson.text: **Superfoods** are foods that may prevent diseases and improve **mental** as well as **physical** health.

examples.text: Blueberries may improve **short-term memory** and **slow the ageing process**.
examples.note: the ageing process = the changes by which we grow old

examples.text: Apples are a good **source** of vitamin C; they can also **lower cholesterol**.
Spinach is high in vitamin A; it can **boost the immune system**.
Vegetable juice, especially tomato, can **reduce the risk** of heart disease.

lesson.heading: Verb + noun collocations worth learning
rows: make growing old happen more slowly
strengthen the body's defences against illness
take the level of cholesterol down
reduce the risk of heart disease
maintain a good level of fitness

lesson.heading: Lifestyle
lesson.text: These extracts from a magazine show the same idea expressed with an adjective and with a noun. Learn both forms together.

examples.text: There has been a **sharp rise** in the number of children who are **obese**. Childhood **obesity** is now a **major** problem.
examples.note: a sharp rise = a sudden, quick increase; obese = extremely fat; major = very big and serious

examples.text: People often do not realise how **stressful** their jobs are. **Stress** can cause high blood pressure and **depression**.
examples.note: depression = a mental illness in which someone is extremely unhappy and anxious for a long period

examples.text: You can **maintain a good level of fitness** with a simple routine of daily exercise.
Alcohol and tobacco are particularly **harmful** if consumed in large quantities. They can cause serious **harm** to the body.

lesson.heading: food or foods? fruit or fruits?
lesson.text: The nouns **food** and **fruit** can be uncountable or countable. Use the uncountable form for food and fruit in general, and the plural only for individual types.

examples.text: That restaurant serves good **food**. I love **fruit**.
We always use **fish** in the singular: Oily **fish** should form part of a healthy diet.

lesson.text: It is **short-term** memory and **long-term** problems - never ~~short-time~~ or ~~long-time~~ in this sense.

exercises.prompt: Would a nutritionist call each of these healthy or not so healthy?

items.text: food with a high salt content
food with a high fat content

exercises.prompt: Match the adjectives with the nouns to make five collocations.
If people eat these foods in large ___, it may be dangerous.
exercises.explanation: *In large quantities* is the usual phrase for talking about how much is consumed.

exercises.prompt: Foods with a high fat ___ may cause health problems.
exercises.explanation: The content of a food is the amount of something that is in it: a high fat content, a high sugar content.

exercises.prompt: Some foods may cause ___ health problems, that is, problems lasting a long time into the future.
exercises.explanation: Long-term means lasting a long time into the future; its opposite here is short-term.

exercises.prompt: Which benefit does each superfood have?

pairs.right: can reduce the risk of heart disease

exercises.prompt: Many fruits are a good ___ of vitamin C.
exercises.explanation: A source is where something comes from - not to be confused with *sauce*.
We say short-term memory: Blueberries can improve short-term memory.

options: Oily fish should form part of a healthy diet.
Oily fishes should form part of a healthy diet.
An oily fishes should form part of a healthy diet.
Oily fishes should form part of an healthy diet.
exercises.explanation: *Fish* is always used in the singular here, just as we say *I love Chinese food*, not *foods*.

exercises.prompt: There has been a sharp ___ in the number of people suffering from depression.
exercises.explanation: A sharp rise is a sudden, quick increase. Note the spelling *depression*.

exercises.prompt: Children who are obese, or who suffer from ___, need to exercise more.
exercises.explanation: The noun from *obese* is *obesity*: childhood obesity is now a major problem.

exercises.prompt: Her job is very ___ and causes her a lot of stress.
exercises.explanation: A job is stressful; the feeling it causes is stress.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order to ask about staying healthy.
exercises.answer: How can we maintain a good level of fitness?
exercises.explanation: *Maintain* is the formal word for *keep*: keep fit / maintain a good level of fitness.
